top.line: 5,664 claims, a frame, eight clusters, one cut, predictions scored
top.para: Twelve readers read 186 articles in half an hour; the validator passed 188 files and 5,664 anchored claims. A frame of 26 ideas emerged before any dimension; without it, eight clusters and a cut of control against the record, control the smaller side. Two predictions held, four in part, four missed.

in-short.line: Built in 9.5 seconds; the join is real; a frame emerged
in-short.para: 188 files derive into 543 pages. 342 shared ids against 48 before; 95% of claims joined. The frame of 26 ideas makes clustering blobs until set aside. The cut is control against the record, control at 43%. Desks mostly hold; the vocabulary has stopped growing; the misses are the finding.

built.line: Twelve parallel readers, one validator, one deterministic build
built.para: Readers took sixteen articles each after the brief was live, twenty to thirty-one minutes, 4.3 million tokens. The result: 188 files, 5,664 claims with 14.5-word quotes, 3,271 edges. fsg.py writes 543 pages and seven JSON files including the whole join as 28,180 typed edges, in 9.5 seconds.

claims.line: Facts and proposals dominate; hypotheses are rare
claims.para: 2,629 facts, 995 data points, 798 limits, 518 proposals, 233 hypotheses, 42 questions. Data points, hypotheses and limits all came in below the predicted shares. Edges are mostly backs and limits; supersedes 19 times, contradicts 13. Every article now has a page that is only its claims.

frame.line: 342 shared ids, and 26 that frame every article
frame.para: The sharing prediction held with room: 342 ids in two or more articles, 95% of claims joined, registries grown to 269 concepts and 664 names. 26 names and ideas appear in over a quarter of all articles, partly by the schema and mostly by the argument; with them in, clusters are two blobs, so they are set aside and listed.

clusters.line: Eight clusters without the frame, mostly matching the desks
clusters.para: The vendors and the risk, the newsroom's method, strategy, memory and policy tooling, regulation and Europe, the browser and the keys, governance as a graph, journalism as intelligence. Agents and policy split three ways; graphs did not merge with vaults. Four desks of five sit 73% or more in two clusters; vaults at 61% is loose.

cut.line: Control against the record, control the smaller side
cut.para: Two cuts agreeing on 88% of nodes put agent security on one side and the newsroom's method on the other. Control is 43%, not the predicted majority. The bridges are the owner, RiskMandate, provenance, sgit, Claude and fractal graphs, not the behaviour policy and the vault, which anchor opposite sides. The map turns in 3D in the page.

peaks.line: Most predicted peaks held; the surprise is the owner
peaks.para: RiskMandate, sgit, the newsroom, Claude, Claude Code, Anthropic, Google and GitHub are peaks; the EU AI Act and OWASP are not. The vault, provenance, the behaviour policy and fractal graphs lead the ideas. The owner, the voice memo and the agents' writing sit at the very top: a reader arrives first at how the newsroom is written.

births.line: The spine is older than the newsroom; growth has stopped
births.para: Of 94 concepts with gravity, 28 were born before September, 32 in September, 9 in early October, 25 since. The 30 newest articles add one new concept each and one in ten is used again. New articles bring new names, 3.4 each, and new claims about old ideas.

dimensions.line: Five dimensions as designed; the peaks needed new words
dimensions.para: Claims, names and vocabulary, sources, time and the editor's layers have their own types and verbs. Gravity, the frame, clusters and the cut are the names dimension counted. The peaks needed arrives_at and overlooks. The kinds and verbs were designed; the frame, clusters, cut, peaks and births were found; the grammar held on all 28,180 edges.

scored.line: Two held, four partly, four missed, in a pattern
scored.para: Claims and the readers' errors missed on the numbers; sharing and sources held; dimensions, clusters, hemispheres, peaks and births held in direction and missed on a number or a name. Content was more stated and older than predicted; the readers more exact: ten quotes refused of 5,664. The method was known better than the material.

readers.line: Five changes the twelve readers agreed on
readers.para: 61 pages have no section anchors; the normaliser rejects quotes with hashes, underscores or backticks; some twins carry reader views above the body; the schema strains on pairs, splits and evidence levels; the registry wanted more seeds, which readers proposed under the same ids. Three are an afternoon's work.

next.line: Expectations for the second run, to be scored
next.para: Fixing anchors should move 1,500 claims off top; a different model should agree on 80% of claim kinds; the frame should hold at 26 give or take three; the eight clusters should hold with new articles moving at most one; control should stay the smaller side. Same clusters means a stable layer.

limits.line: One model, one run, three choices, a frame partly schematic
limits.para: No second model checked the files. The frame is partly the schema's doing and partly the argument's. Clusters depend on the gravity rule, the normalised weights and removing the frame. The peak score is one formula. 61 articles lack anchors. Cost is in tokens. This article has no file yet, and this is one run of two.

sources.line: The memo, the brief, report.json, the readers' reports
sources.para: The owner's memo and the morning's brief; every number from graphs/data/report.json written by fsg.py from the 188 files; the readers' closing reports and token counts from the session; the grammar from graphs.sgit.ai; the gravity rule and the Historian's count from two earlier articles. Louvain and the Fiedler cut written into the build.
